description: We are Devil's Triangle, a passionate and driven team participating in this year's NASA challenge. We are deeply fascinated by space exploration, cutting-edge technology, aerospace engineering, and creative problem-solving. Our mission is to combine scientific rigor with bold, innovative thinking to tackle real-world space and technology problems.
summary: LUNAVIS is an interactive 3D decision-support web application designed to evaluate and compare lunar landing sites and mission windows at the Moon's South Pole. Inspired by real-world mission challenges like the 2025 Athena lander-where rough terrain and prolonged shadows cut operations short-our tool bridges the gap between fragmented NASA datasets (LOLA DEM, JPL Horizons) and actionable mission planning. By simulating local terrain occlusion, solar illumination, and Earth line-of-sight over time, LUNAVIS helps mission planners, NewSpace startups, insurers, and STEM educators quickly screen out high-risk landing scenarios and identify sustainable operational windows before launch.
details:
How It Works & Key Features: LUNAVIS unifies spatial terrain modeling and temporal celestial mechanics into a single three-step decision-support workflow (Explore – Analyze – Compare):

1. Terrain-Aware Horizon & Line-of-Sight Engine: Rather than relying on ideal flat-horizon ephemerides, our Python backend (horizon_v2 & lunar_model) processes high-resolution Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) Digital Elevation Models (up to 5 m/pixel) combined with wide-area DEMs to compute 360-degree local horizon profiles. It then cross-references these profiles with hourly Sun and Earth azimuth/elevation vectors from NASA JPL Horizons to accurately calculate solar power availability and direct-to-Earth (DTE) communication windows.

2. Spatio-Temporal Trade-off Analysis: Users can evaluate how shifting a mission launch date by just a few days impacts operational survival. For instance, our case study demonstrates that moving a 7-day mission window by 5 days at the same candidate site can drop sunlight availability from 100% to 69.6% and introduce a 51-hour continuous darkness gap.

3. Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (MCDA) & Interactive 3D Globe: Built with React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and CesiumJS, the frontend renders an interactive 3D lunar globe where users can inspect elevation, slope, and illumination timelines, and compare candidate sites side-by-side using configurable mission risk thresholds.

Tools, Languages & Technologies Used:

- Backend & Scientific Computing: Python, NumPy, SciPy, Rasterio/GeoTIFF processing, custom multi-scale horizon ray-tracing engine, and an automated verification suite (215 unit and formula-audit tests passed)

- Frontend & 3D Visualization: React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, and CesiumJS.

- Data Sources: NASA JPL Horizons API and LRO/LOLA DEM datasets.

Creativity, Benefits & Intended Impact: Most existing planetary tools are either map viewers lacking temporal mission-window scoring or raw orbital calculators inaccessible to non-specialists. LUNAVIS bridges this gap with a transparent, explainable scoring layer that transforms raw lunar datasets into clear operational insights. Beyond assisting mission planners at space agencies and commercial CLPS/NewSpace companies with rapid early-stage site shortlisting, LUNAVIS provides data-backed risk due diligence for space investors and insurers, and serves as an interactive 3D virtual lab for STEM education. Committed to scientific integrity, the system explicitly labels conditional assumptions and unverified terrain states rather than overstating certainty.
